nodes.title: Close distinct integers give the required positive odd parameters
Hermite–Lindemann implies the diagonal logarithm-square conclusion
nodes.lean_statement: (∀ z : ℂ, z ≠ 0 → IsAlgebraic ℚ z → Transcendental ℚ (Complex.exp z)) → ∀ m : ℤ, m ≠ -1 → m ≠ 0 → Irrational ((Real.log (1 + 1 / (m : ℝ))) ^ 2)

nodes.title: Integer-relation criterion and invariance under the real embedding
nodes.lean_statement: ∀ (d : ℕ) (v : Fin d → ℝ), (LinearIndependent ℚ v ↔ ∀ a : Fin d → ℤ, (∑ i : Fin d, (a i : ℝ) * v i) = 0 → ∀ i, a i = 0) ∧ (LinearIndependent ℚ (fun i : Fin d => (v i : ℂ)) ↔ LinearIndependent ℚ v)

nodes.title: Four-term independence forces product irrationality
nodes.lean_statement: ∀ x y : ℝ, LinearIndependent ℚ ![1, x, y, x * y] → Irrational (x * y)

nodes.title: Close distinct integers have the same sign and quantitative magnitude bounds
Same-sign integers yield odd absolute parameters with controlled gap and size
nodes.lean_statement: ∀ (m n L : ℤ), 0 < m * n → L ≤ |m| → L ≤ |n| → let a : ℤ := max |2 * m + 1| |2 * n + 1|; let b : ℤ := min |2 * m + 1| |2 * n + 1|; Odd a ∧ Odd b ∧ a - b = 2 * |m - n| ∧ 2 * L - 1 ≤ b

nodes.title: Integer reciprocal arguments are positive and different from one
